take: Crude breaking $100 with the US striking five Iran-linked tankers and Tehran claiming two US vessels hit is the dominant story, and with Hormuz passage declining it directly threatens the roughly 20m b/d of seaborne crude and product flows through the Strait, keeping both flat price and crack spreads elevated. The Greek-owned VLCC New Andros, carrying around 2m barrels of Iraqi fuel oil, was struck by a drone in Iraqi waters, whilst Peninsula confirmed a fatality and a missing crew member from an incident off Dubai, so war-risk premia and freight rates on Gulf loadings should normalise higher across crude and product tankers. The inventory angle is thin but supportive, with the API estimating US crude stocks fell 300,000 barrels in the week ending 4 September, a modest draw that reinforces the bullish tone rather than driving it. The cross-market link to watch is bunker versus gasoil, as LNG bunkering expands with Titan loading 11,000 m3 at Klaipeda and Burando entering Norway, but the marginal tonne remains oil-based and will reprice with distillate cracks. In the next 24 hours watch for confirmation of further Hormuz transits halting, any US or Iranian escalation, and the official EIA inventory print to validate the API draw.
